name: wherefore

palette.none: the engine has no brand: the colours in this tree are the map's default theme in graph.py, the fixture company's, and the release pictures' - none of them a fact about Wherefore

note: This repository as a client of the engine it holds. Its README is generated from a template, the commands and the principles, each said once in src/wherefore/; everything else is authored or test data. It is judged by the previous release (requirements-engine.txt), never by the code being edited.

commands.why: every command the CLI has, and what each does: the CLI's help prints it and the README is generated from it

principles.why: the principles the engine enforces: the README is generated from it, and the company's site reads it from the release it pins

generators.makes: README.md, from docs/README.template.md, the commands, the features and the principles

inventory.note: Every tracked file is generated, authored or captured. GENERATED is derived by running the generators - README.md, here - and never declared; this declares the rest.

rules: code: the engine, its tests and proofs, the recorded moves, and this corpus's generator and checks. A person writes it; nothing generates it
the design records, the changelog, the skill and the README's template - written by a person. Not README.md, which corpus/readme.py writes
the commands, said once: the source the CLI's help and the README are made from
the principles, said once: the source the README and the company's site state them from
what the engine does, as features, said once: the source the README lists and the company's site must say each of

every release, said once as data, with a picture of it working: the source the company's changelog page is built from; tests/test_releases.py holds it to CHANGELOG.md and runs the newest picture again
the workflow wherefore init writes into a client - its own watch for the engine's releases - shipped as package data and the client's from then on

the roadmap, beside the code: what is next and what is later, said once, for the people and agents working here and for the company's site, which copies it; tests/test_roadmap.py fails an item the engine already ships
the fixture company's corpus - the engine's test data. It is a corpus of its own, held by its own wherefore.json and gate in tests/test_phase5.py, not by this one
the package: its name, version and dependencies
what the sdist carries besides the package: the tests' helpers and fixture, so its tests run
the licence, Apache-2.0, exactly as the Apache Software Foundation publishes it
this file: what this repository is to the engine
the release that judges this corpus - the previous one, never the tree being edited
